note.text:
Light travels in straight lines (rectilinear propagation). A ray is drawn as a straight line with an arrow; a beam is a bundle of rays: parallel (from the sun or a torch with a reflector), convergent (coming together) or divergent (spreading out from a small source).
An opaque object in the path of light makes a shadow. With a point source, the shadow is sharp (umbra only); with a large source there is a dark umbra and a lighter penumbra.
With a point source, the shadow on the screen is bigger than the object: shadow height = object height × (source-to-screen distance ÷ source-to-object distance).

worked_example.problem: An object {h} cm tall is {d1} cm from a point source. The screen is {d2} cm from the source. Find the height of the shadow.
steps: Light travels in straight lines, so the shadow grows in proportion to the distance.

example: Light from a candle spreads out: divergent.

cards.idea: Shadow height = object height × (screen distance ÷ object distance).

check.prompt: An object {h} cm tall is {d1} cm from a point source of light. The screen is {d2} cm from the source. Find the height of the shadow.

misconceptions.explain: The shadow is bigger than the object: the rays spread out.
Divide the screen distance by the object distance, not the other way.

solution: Shadow = object height × (source to screen ÷ source to object).

pick.q: Why do opaque objects make shadows?
pick.r: light travels in straight lines and cannot bend round them
w: light is absorbed by the air
e: Darkness is the absence of light.

pick.q: What is a ray of light?
pick.r: the straight path that light follows, drawn with an arrow
e: A shadow is where light does not reach.
pick.y: Rays are drawn as straight lines with arrows.

pick.q: Light spreading out from a candle flame
pick.y: Spreading rays make a divergent beam.

e: The sun is very far: its rays are almost parallel.

pick.q: Light coming together after a magnifying glass
pick.y: Rays coming together make a convergent beam.
